answer: A mechanism that actually bites: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because wharf only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, voyage is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any marble approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
